newsitem.title: CROATIA: Serb refugees head home across Croatia.
newsitem.headline: Serb refugees head home across Croatia.

text.p: Serb refugees returned in a convoy of tractors and trailers on Thursday to homes they fled in 1995 when a Croatian army offensive recaptured territory from rebel Serbs.
Around 70 Serbs, most of them elderly but also including a few young families, made the journey back to villages in central Croatia from eastern Slavonia where they had lived in exile.
The refugees were driven most of the way home in buses with their tractors following on U.N. trucks, which were disembarked at a parking lot for the last stage.
Nikola Marjanovic, 67, and his wife then spluttered along the main highway linking Croatia's capital city Zagreb with the Adriatic coast in their rusty old tractor.
When he arrived home, Marjanovic was faced with a wrecked house with no windows or doors.
"We lost two years of our lives, I'm glad to be back home now," he said. Marjanovic said he would receive a pension from the Croatian government and hoped for some money to help repair his house.
His neighbours rushed out to greet him with hugs and smiles. They were refugees from Travnik, in central Bosnia, who had been rehoused in the village a couple of years ago after fleeing themselves.

Altogether 30 families returned home on Thursday. The resettlement will be the first of a long line of such operations as Serbs living in Eastern Slavonia head back to villages in the south and west of Croatia.
Some 2,100 Serb families are expected to leave Eastern Slavonia and return to former rebel parts of Croatia, while some 40,000 Croats are expected to head back into the region.

Several Serbs who returned home earlier this year were attacked by bitter Bosnian Croat refugees who didn't want to live with their former enemies. However a United Nations worker told Reuters there had been fewer incidents recently since Zagreb tried to calm the violence.
Zagreb says it wants to encourage Serbs to return home to vacate the houses of Croats in Eastern Slavonia.
